create.name: Lyla June
create.bio:
Lyla June Johnston is a musician, poet, scholar and organiser whose ancestry is Diné (Navajo) and Tsétsêhéstâhese (Cheyenne) as well as European. She grew up within a traditional Diné outlook, went on to study human ecology at Stanford and Indigenous education at graduate level, and completed a doctorate at the University of Alaska Fairbanks on how Indigenous nations across the Americas tended land to create abundant food for people and animals alike.

Her talks and songs move between ecology, history and prayer. She speaks about the land-care knowledge of her ancestors, about forgiveness and non-violence, and about helping people of every background, Europeans included, reconnect with the earth-based ways of their own forebears; in Diné, she points out, a single word holds both song and prayer. She has spoken at TEDx Kansas City, Bioneers, Science and Nonduality and Wisdom 2.0, has taken part in Kripalu's online series centring Indigenous voices, and has released several albums of original music. With Joy De Vito she created Lifting Hearts off the Ground, a book of 46 poems answering the articles of the UN Declaration on the Rights of Indigenous Peoples.
